skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface owned by other batches; the one ledger correction this reading supports is proposed through the intake note rather than edited.
A patient genotype-phenotype report supplies no therapeutic lever for the reference genotype class; forging hypotheses from one case would manufacture a lead.
No compound is tested as an intervention with a measured outcome beyond clinical anecdote, so there is no molecule to send to BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; every change is proposed as a commit candidate for a later BATCH_COMMIT.
The triples are published in the candidates for a blind auditor; the reader of a paper cannot audit their own locators.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-02: Zara F[au] 608, Zara F[au] AND WWOX 2. An epilepsy-genetics group (clinical plus molecular: exome, fibroblast RT-PCR, qPCR, array-CGH) with a prior WWOX mouse/organoid paper. The molecular resolution is strong; the 'phenotypic-driven' diagnostic claim is a single-case narrative.

entries.proposition: Exome CNV analysis missed the single-exon deletion.
entries.snippet: No other potentially pathogenic variants were identified in the exome. CNVs analysis was also unremarkable.

entries.proposition: The exon 6 deletion's transcript consequence was measured in patient fibroblast RNA.
entries.snippet: The RT-PCR derived from fibroblast extracts of patient and unaffected parents and age-matched neurotypical control

experimental_context.genotype: p.Arg264* / exon 6 deletion; carrier parents; control
experimental_context.endpoint: RT-PCR exon4F-exon7R product and Sanger junction

entries.proposition: Measured junction: exon 5 fused to exon 7 (RT-PCR product sequenced).

entries.snippet: Several anti-seizure medications (ASM) were ineffective (i.e., valproate, vigabatrin, clonazepam, clobazam, levetiracetam, rufinamide, and CBD oil)

entries.proposition: Phenobarbital and nitrazepam are reported for adverse events, not as ineffective.
entries.snippet: or determined adverse events such as extreme drowsiness or increased secretions (i.e., phenobarbital, nitrazepam)

entries.proposition: Vigabatrin, listed as ineffective, remains among the current medications.
The earliest-onset claim; day-1 onset had already been reported in the Piard 2019 series.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, our patient had the earliest epilepsy onset, presenting on the first day of life

entries.proposition: Early imaging includes a small inferior vermis.
entries.snippet: frontal bilateral periventricular cysts, enlargement of cerebral subarachnoid spaces, especially in the frontal-temporal regions, and a small inferior vermis

entries.proposition: The late leukoencephalopathy pattern is offered as a question, not a diagnostic sign.
entries.snippet: more studies are needed to verify if this periventricular leukomalacia-like pattern is a typical feature of the disease

entries.proposition: MRI at 4 months: periventricular cysts, delayed myelination, thin corpus callosum, inferior vermis hypoplasia; MRS lactate peak.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2 A-G: axial/coronal T2 with arrows at frontal periventricular cysts; sagittal T1 thick arrow (corpus callosum) and arrowhead (inferior vermis); spectrum with lactate doublet arrow.

entries.proposition: MRI at 2 years 4 months: posterior periventricular white-matter loss and signal change, squared ventricles, pons and dentate T2/FLAIR hyperintensity, inferior vermis hypoplasia; reduced NAA, no lactate.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3 A-M: T2/FLAIR series with empty arrows at posterior periventricular white matter, arrows at pons, arrowheads at dentate nuclei; sagittal T1 arrowhead at inferior vermis; spectrum without lactate.
